findings.description: src/fault_manager.c fm_submit discards a report when the 36-entry pending queue is full. The design does not establish that arrivals and drain time prevent loss or late submission under SWC-SUP-008.
findings.requested_change: Provide a bounded arrival and service argument that establishes report capacity and deadlines, or revise the reporting design so detections are not discarded.

findings.description: SWC-SUP-061 and OP-SWC-011 leave the T_DIAG flow rule unresolved. The design checks at the 5 ms cycle-end phase although T_DIAG may execute within its 20 ms limit, so a timely execution can be reported as a missing checkpoint.
findings.requested_change: Obtain the product decision and align the flow check and timing design with it.

findings.description: src/time_service.c initializes its accumulated timestamp from timer value zero. OP-SWU-014 records that the inputs do not establish that the timer runs from reset or that hal_timer_start preserves it, so the reset-relative origin required by SWC-SUP-012 and SWR-DIA-003 is unestablished.
findings.requested_change: Establish a supported reset-relative time source and its initialization contract, then align the unit and port.

findings.description: OP-SWU-011 records that the core clock, CRC throughput and execution times are unavailable. The design cannot substantiate the SWC-SUP-061 execution allocations, the 0.5 ms CRC segment limit or the supervisor processor-time budget.
findings.requested_change: Obtain the missing platform and execution-time evidence and establish the task and processor-time budgets.

findings.description: src/cycle_task.c reports a refused window-watchdog enable as fault code 9 with entity WWDG. CON-SUP-119 specifies CONFIG as the entity for code 9, so this path produces a report inconsistent with the product decision.
findings.requested_change: Resolve the watchdog-enable failure classification against the requirements and make the reported code and entity consistent with the accepted decision.
